title: Windows podman.exe built with Go 1.27.1 crashes at startup ("unexpected return pc" / "unknown caller pc")
body:
### Issue Description

Windows `podman.exe` v6.1.2 and v6.1.3 crash at startup with a Go runtime fatal error, before `main` runs. `podman --version` crashed 98 of 100 times. Both releases were built with Go 1.27.1 (`go-version: stable` in the release workflow). Go 1.27.0 and 1.27.1 have a Windows thread-creation bug, golang/go#81731. The fix is CL 841305, planned for Go 1.27.2 (not released yet). v6.1.0, built with Go 1.26.5, ran clean 100 of 100 times.

I confirmed the cause with a controlled build. I built v6.1.2 from source twice with the same flags. Only one file in the Go toolchain differed:

- go1.27.1: `--version` crashed 100 of 100 times.
- go1.27.1 + CL 841305: 0 of 100. `machine list` and `ps -a` also worked.

The crash happens on every command because the vendored `BurntSushi/toml` reads the local time zone in `init`. On Windows that calls `LockOSThread` inside the standard library, which is the path the Go fix changes.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Install podman v6.1.2 or v6.1.3 for Windows.
2. In PowerShell, run `podman --version` about 20 times.

### Describe the results you received

```
runtime: g 3: unexpected return pc for runtime.gopark called from 0xffffffffffffffff
...
fatal error: unknown caller pc
runtime.scanstack > runtime.markroot.func1 > runtime.gcDrain > runtime.gcBgMarkWorker.func2
```

### Describe the results you expected

`podman --version` prints the version.

### podman info output

```yaml
# podman info cannot run: the client crashes first.
client: podman.exe v6.1.2 (go1.27.1, windows/amd64), Podman Desktop 1.29.3
os: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (24 logical processors)
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes (v6.1.3, 98 of 100 runs crashed)

### Additional information

Request: build the Windows release with Go 1.26.5 until Go 1.27.2 is out. `release-build-artifacts.yml` has `go-version: stable` in three places at v6.1.3.

Workarounds: run `wsl -d podman-machine-default -u root podman ps -a`, or use v6.1.0.

I tested one machine only. Build commands, hashes, crash counts, a full crash dump and the call chain are in https://gist.github.com/ljcadungog/23539ae34ad350b891c1eb90a63cdedc.

*Prepared with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Anthropic) through Claude Code, on behalf of @ljcadungog, who reviewed it.*
